summary.oneLiner: Ahmedabad-based vertically integrated cotton textile manufacturer producing grey fabric and yarn through in-house weaving and spinning.
summary.business: Alpine Texworld manufactures Grey Fabric and Yarn and provides yarn-sizing job work, operating a weaving unit (112 Toyota air-jet looms) and a spinning unit (open-end rotor) in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, plus a 72-loom weaving unit through its subsidiary Alpine Cottweave LLP. It sells predominantly to fabric processors/traders in Gujarat, and has pursued backward integration into yarn to reduce reliance on third-party yarn purchases.

endMarkets: Domestic textile processors/traders, predominantly Gujarat (~97% of revenue); minor sales to Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, Delhi, Haryana

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Backward integration: set up in-house spinning (Manufacturing Unit 2, Mar 2025) to produce yarn used as input for grey fabric, reducing reliance on third-party yarn purchases; acquired 97% of Alpine Cottweave LLP (weaving) to add capacity. Units are adjacent to minimise logistics cost. Company continues to also source yarn from third parties.

customers.title: Oem (RHP)
customers.body:
- Toyota (air-jet looms)
- Picanol NV (air-jet looms)
- Karl Mayer Textilmaschinen Ag (sizing)
- Saurer Intelligent Technology Ag (spinning)

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Grey fabric is ~96-97% of revenue; margin sensitive to cotton/yarn price volatility
- Backward integration into yarn (Unit 2, FY25) to cushion raw-material cost swings
- Subsidy (Other Operating) income ~Rs 40 mn/yr in revenue
- High working-capital and debt intensity (D/E 2.35x FY26); capex-heavy investing cash flows

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: Setting up Proposed Manufacturing Unit 3 (48 additional looms, +77.50 lakh metres/annum grey fabric, ~28% capacity increase) on company-owned land at Survey No. 1098 adjacent to existing units, targeted for commercial production by March 2027 and funded from the fresh issue. Separately, an additional spinning-and-weaving unit is planned to be funded via debt and internal accruals.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- Vertically integrated (spinning + weaving + sizing) reducing reliance on third-party yarn
- Located in Ahmedabad/Gujarat cotton belt with ready raw-material access
- High capacity utilisation (weaving 107% consol FY26, spinning 88.5%)
- Captive solar (rooftop + ground-mounted, ~10 MW aggregate) reducing power cost
- Experienced promoters (25+ years in textiles)

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Top 10 customers = 70.33% of FY26 revenue, no firm long-term contracts
- ~97% of revenue from Gujarat
- Grey fabric ~96-97% of revenue
- Consolidated borrowings Rs 1,777.61 mn, D/E 2.35x FY26; unsecured related-party loans Rs 324.37 mn repayable on demand
- Cotton/yarn is the dominant input; margins exposed to price swings
- Unit 2 operated without GPCB Consolidated Consent & Authorisation; delayed CS appointment; RoC filing discrepancies
- Land purchased from promoter/promoter-group at consideration below market value; personal guarantees by promoters

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Set up Proposed Manufacturing Unit 3 (48 looms) to add grey-fabric weaving capacity, funded from IPO net proceeds**
- **Increase installed weaving capacity by 77.50 lakh metres/annum (~28.08% of existing) via Unit 3**
- **Prepay/repay outstanding borrowings from net proceeds to improve debt-equity ratio**
- **Commence commercial production at Proposed Manufacturing Unit 3**
- **Establish additional spinning-and-weaving unit (beyond Unit 3) funded through debt and internal accruals**

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Increase weaving capacity by installing 48 looms at Proposed Manufacturing Unit 3 (IPO funded)
- Further backward integration and additional spinning/weaving unit funded by debt + internal accruals
- Acquire adjacent land parcels to scale operations
- Expand renewable (solar) energy footprint to lower costs
